# Chat exports — sorted by theme

[Permalink: Chat exports — sorted by theme](https://github.com/UselessMoron123/all-my-chats/blob/main/chat-themes.md#chat-exports--sorted-by-theme)

All **235 chats** (470 files: each chat has a `.json` and a `.txt` export, paired via their conversation URL) are extracted and sorted into theme folders under `chats/`.

The original archives remain at the repo root if you want them back verbatim.

Folders are numbered by size (01 = biggest). Classification is keyword-based on full titles, so treat it as approximate.

| Folder | Chats | Share | Contents |
| --- | --: | --: | --- |
| `chats/13-Other-stray-questions/` | 5 | 2% | One-off trivia/translation questions that fit no theme. |
| `chats/12-RimWorld/` | 3 | 1% | RimWorld simulator RP + ideal starting pawn stats. |
| `chats/11-Creative-writing/` | 4 | 2% | Monty Python-style dialogue, Roman citizen diary, scene descriptions, text rewriting. |
| `chats/10-Shrek-RP/` | 5 | 2% | Several restarts of a "before chapter 1, not near the swamp" Shrek roleplay. |
| `chats/09-Skyrim-TES-RP/` | 5 | 2% | Skyrim roleplays incl. a Breton isekai and a min-max strategy chat. |
| `chats/08-Meta-about-the-agent/` | 6 | 3% | "What are you", agent capabilities, checking the chat exports themselves, using agent mode from a phone. |
| `chats/07-Spore-RP/` | 7 | 3% | Repeated attempts at a Spore cell-to-space RPG with slow stage progression. |
| `chats/06-Web-forum-fanfic-lookups/` | 10 | 4% | Asking the agent to read pages/forums (Paradox forum, Habr, YouTube), find fanfics, search VK/kubikus, or just reply "прочитал" to pasted text. |
| `chats/05-Game-dev-money/` | 11 | 5% | Solo browser/mobile game ideas, reviving an old wap game, Yandex Games monetization, crypto/AI-agent earning questions. |
| `chats/04-Kenshi/` | 17 | 7% | Route planning from Hub over numbered maps, recruiting lists (free recruits, ≤3000 cost), town checklists, beginner "what do I do first" questions. |
| `chats/03-Game-simulator-RPs/` | 18 | 8% | "Let's roleplay, I want an X simulator" chats: Minecraft, Zomboid, ant colony, cult, Mafia, Harry Potter, peasant sim — plus Sims 4, Stardew Valley, V Rising, Oregon Trail. |
| `chats/02-Original-isekai-RPs/` | 21 | 9% | Original scenario roleplays: medieval/Roman settings, isekai (попаданец) jumps (Pirates of the Caribbean, time travel, Duck Tales), the recurring "Ray" narration series. |
| `chats/01-CK2-CK3/` | 123 | 52% | The dominant theme. Parsing/sorting CK2 trait & character game files, bloodline grouping, councillor/dynasty names, hypotheticals, plus AAR/литстрим writing about dynasties. |

     - `Let's roleplay. I want an interactive story_litrpg...` (Messages 3, 5)
     - `Roleplay. I was isekaied in rimworld...` (Messages 3, 5)
     - `Think of a rimworld scenario for me...` (Message 3)
     - `We're going to roleplay as each isekaied into skyrim...` (Message 3)
     - `Давай проведём ролеплей. В стиле подземелий и драконов...` (Message 3)
     - `Я хочу ролеплей в мире марвел...` (Message 3)
2. **35 AI-written files (`tool-write_file`) & 19 file edits (`tool-edit_file`)**:
   - In `.json`, `tool-write_file` contains the full `input.content` of every file the agent created for you (e.g., `/home/user/plan-kripto-zarabotka.md`, `/home/user/All-about-cool-AI/план-заработка.md`, `/home/user/slmp/SLMP_Windows_гайд.md`, `/home/user/slmp/Как_сделать_образ_самому.md`, `/home/user/quintus_channel.md`, `/home/user/summary_miki_billi.md`, `/home/user/character_questionnaires.md`, `/home/user/ducktales/00-ПРАВИЛА-ИГРЫ.md`, `character_sheet.md`, `rimworld_pawns.md`, etc.).
   - In `.txt`, `formatAgentPartAsText` only wrote `[tool: write_file]\npath: ...\nstatus: success` and omitted `input.content` (and `old_text` / `new_text` for `tool-edit_file`).
3. **User file attachments (`part.type === "file"`) & `tool-bash` stdout/stderr**:
   - Two user-uploaded images (`novasurvivalgame_2026-09-17-22-16-21_1789672581690.webp` and `SmallMarked.png`) and `tool-bash` `stdout`/`stderr` outputs were present in `.json` but omitted in `.txt`.

#### B. Next.js Flight `$f0`–`$ff` / `$f00`–`$fff` Hex Reference Bug in 2 Huge Agent `.json` Files
- In `resolveNextFlightReferences`, the reference regex `/^\$(?:L|@|S|F|Q|W)?([0-9a-f]+)$/i` included `F` in the optional prefix group with the case-insensitive `/i` flag.
- Because `f` is also a hexadecimal digit, any Next.js Flight `:T` text chunk whose hex ID had 2+ digits starting with `f` (`$f0`–`$ff` at chunks 240–255, and `$f00`–`$fff` at chunks 3840–4095) had its leading `f` stripped as a prefix:
  - Only **2 of the 41 chats** had enough tool calls (`> 240` large strings) to reach hex ID `$f0`:
    1. `arena-agent-Модешь поискать в кубикусе сообщение от пользователя Ara-2026-09-29T19-22-27-742Z.json` (which has ~1,900 tool calls and ~3,880 `:T` chunks):
       - In Message 3 (parts 51–58, chunks `$f0`–`$ff`) and Message 26 (parts 117–139, chunks `$f00`–`$f39`), stripping the leading `f` turned `$f00`–`$f0f` into `$00`–`$0f` (left unresolved as `"$f00"`–`"$f0f"`) and turned `$f10`–`$f39` into `$10`–`$39`.
       - In particular, in Message 26 Part 133 Result 4, `"$f25"` had its `"f"` stripped to `"25"`, which matched `rowRecords["25"]` (the root Agent payload row itself), embedding a duplicate 5 MB copy of the raw Agent payload inside that search result and bloating the file to 33.8 MB.
    2. `arena-agent-Найди фанфик _ggwp r__ Будущее, человек тестер виртуальн-2026-09-29T19-22-42-016Z.json` (which has 257 large strings):
       - 13 `tool-fetch_page` / `tool-web_search` parts in Messages 7, 9, 11, and 12 (chunks `$f0`–`$ff`) resolved to top-level Flight rows `0`–`f` instead of `:T` text chunks `f0`–`ff`.
  - All other 39 Agent `.json` files had `< 240` `:T` chunks and were completely unaffected.

---

### 3. Fixes Applied to `Arena.ai - LMSYS Arena Chat Exporter-2.2.user.js` (and Pushed to PR #1)

1. **Fixed `$fxx` / `$fxxx` Hex Reference Resolution**:
   - Changed the reference matcher in `resolveNextFlightReferences` to `/^\$(?:L|@)?([0-9a-f]+)$/i` (removing `F|S|Q|W` from the prefix group so hex digits `a–f` are never consumed as prefixes), filtered out `I[...]` / `HL[...]` / React VDOM `["$", ...]` rows from `rowRecords`, and seeded `activeStack` with `new Set([rowId])` so no row can ever inline itself.
2. **Complete `.txt` Formatting for All Agent Parts & Attachments**:
   - Added full formatting in `formatAgentPartAsText` for:
     - `data-tool-results` (renders all `ask_user` user answers — verified **0 `(empty)` messages** across all 41 Agent chats),
     - `tool-ask_user` (renders all questions and option labels/descriptions),
     - `tool-write_file` (includes full `content`),
     - `tool-edit_file` (includes `old_text` and `new_text`),
     - `tool-bash` (includes `exit_code`, `stdout`, and `stderr`),
     - `file` parts and `experimental_attachments` (includes filename, media type, and URL).

results.description:
# How to Install 7-Zip on Debian 13, 12 and 11
## Install 7-Zip on Debian with APT
| Method | Channel | What You Get | Updates | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| APT Package Manager | Debian Repos | Debian-maintained package for your release | APT-managed updates | Most users who want simple maintenance |
| Manual Binary | GitHub Releases | Latest upstream 7zz binary | Manual replacement or helper script | Users who need newest features or upstream RAR/RAR5 support | ## Install 7-Zip from Official Binary on Debian
If you need the latest version, upstream RAR/RAR5 extraction, or 7-Zip without root access, download the official binary directly from the 7-Zip GitHub releases page. The upstream tarball includes the 7zz binary (and 7zzs), always uses the 7zz command, and keeps format support independent from Debian’s package splits. ### Download the Latest 7-Zip Release
```bash
release_json=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/ip7z/7zip/releases/latest)
download_url=$(printf '%s\n' "$release_json" | awk -F'"' '/browser_download_url/ && /linux-x64/ && /tar.xz/ {print $4; exit}')

if [ -n "$download_url" ]; then
  archive_name=${download_url##*/}
  wget -O "$archive_name" "$download_url"
else
  printf 'No linux-x64 tarball found. Check the 7-Zip releases page.\n' >&2
fi
``` This sequence fetches the latest release metadata, extracts the x64 Linux tarball URL, stores the upstream filename in archive_name, and downloads the tarball. It also fails visibly when GitHub cannot be reached or the expected asset name changes.

```
Alpine's 7zip package compiles the RAR codec out, so T074's six-format
acceptance criterion could not pass against the image as built. The
owner decided to keep .rar: the image will ship upstream's static
7zzs, fetched from the pinned tarball and verified by SHA-256 (the
ADR-0018 mechanism), installed as /usr/local/bin/7zz. Verified today:
7z2603-linux-x64's 7zzs is ET_EXEC with no PT_INTERP and lists Rar/Rar5
formats with Rar1-Rar5 codecs.

This change is the decision record and plan repair only: ADR-0021,
the decisions index, the resolved open question in doc 06, the
IMPLEMENTING.md note, and T074's Files table/steps/acceptance now
cover Dockerfile, internal/config/config.go, the checked-in .rar
fixture under internal/jobs/testdata/, and the two docs whose stated
default moves to /usr/local/bin/7zz. The blocked record stays for
history. Implementation of the runtime change rides with T074.

results.description:
# How to Install 7-Zip on Fedora 44
## Install 7-Zip on Fedora Linux
### Choose a 7-Zip Installation Method on Fedora
| Method | Source | Main Command | Update Behavior | Best For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DNF standard package | Fedora repositories | 7z | Included in sudo dnf upgrade --refresh | Most compression, extraction, listing, testing, and encryption tasks |
| DNF standalone all package | Fedora repositories | 7zz | Included in sudo dnf upgrade --refresh | Users who want Fedora’s packaged 7zz command |
| Official upstream binary | 7-Zip download page and GitHub releases | 7zz | Manual replacement or helper script | Newest upstream release, RAR/RAR5 extraction, or no-DNF environments | ## Install Official 7-Zip 7zz Binary on Fedora Linux
### Resolve the Official 7-Zip Release Asset
Resolve the current Linux tarball URL and SHA-256 digest from the official 7-Zip GitHub release metadata. The 7-Zip download page links to these Linux release assets, while GitHub exposes the digest used for verification. ```bash
resolve_7zip_asset() {
    if [ -z "${SEVENZIP_ARCH:-}" ]; then
        printf 'SEVENZIP_ARCH is not set; run the architecture detection step first.\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi

    release_json="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/ip7z/7zip/releases/latest)"
    if ! asset_info="$(
        RELEASE_JSON="$release_json" ARCH_TAG="linux-${SEVENZIP_ARCH}" python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import os
import sys

release = json.loads(os.environ["RELEASE_JSON"])
arch = os.environ["ARCH_TAG"]
for asset in release.get("assets", []):
    name = asset.get("name", "")
    if name.startswith("7z") and name.endswith(f"{arch}.tar.xz"):
        digest = asset.get("digest") or ""
        if digest.startswith("sha256:"):
            digest = digest.split(":", 1)[1]
        if not digest:

parts.text:
**Короткий вывод:** в опубликованном архиве `all-my-chats` все сессии из исходного списка теперь учтены, включая Agent Mode. Но TXT-экспорты всё ещё теряют часть содержимого, а проверить именно последнюю версию вашего экспортёра по `Desktop.rar` не получилось: в нём страницы для примера, а не результат экспорта.

Я нашёл чат [«look in repo. i managed to export my chats…»](https://arena.ai/agent/01a0ee40-fd55-7ead-a85d-5ea62e03cbe8). В нём разбирались прежняя потеря 40 Agent Mode-сессий и последующие исправления экспортёра.

### Что сошлось

В `all-my-chats/main` я независимо проверил содержимое папки `chats/`:

- **235 JSON и 235 TXT**: 194 обычные сессии и 41 Agent Mode.
- У всех 235 уникальных URL есть пара JSON/TXT; дубликатов и непарных файлов нет.
- Все 234 записи из исходного списка названий нашлись; есть ещё одна дополнительная тестовая сессия.
- Все JSON разбираются, а число сообщений в заголовках TXT совпадает с JSON. Пустых Agent-сообщений и пустых строк-маркеров `(empty)` в TXT не обнаружил.

То есть **сам факт пропуска Agent Mode-сессий в опубликованном архиве устранён**.

### Что всё ещё теряется в TXT

В уже опубликованных TXT и в доступном коде v2.2 формат TXT не сохраняет некоторые данные инструментов, хотя они есть в JSON:

- результаты `fetch_page`: 371 блока, около **2,56 млн символов**;
- содержимое `read_file`: 20 блоков, около **357 тыс. символов**;
- описания результатов `web_search`; кроме того, для 547 вызовов TXT показывает только первые 8 результатов, пропуская **1 070** остальных.

При этом содержимое 35 `write_file` и 48 фрагментов `edit_file` в TXT нашлось; непустые reasoning-блоки тоже присутствуют. Ещё 18 выводов `bash` уже помечены в JSON как обрезанные на стороне инструмента — экспортёр не сможет восстановить то, чего Arena ему не передала. Два вложения представлены ссылками и метаданными, но сами файлы внутрь архива не вложены.

**Практический итог:** JSON выглядит хорошим основным архивом; TXT — удобное, но не полностью без потерь представление.

### Что удалось проверить по `Desktop.rar`

Архив целый: проверка CRC прошла. В нём 3 основные сохранённые HTML-страницы и ресурсы сайта, **но нет JSON/TXT-результатов экспортёра**. На страницах панель экспорта показывает состояние `Ready`, а не завершённый экспорт. Парсер из исторической версии v2.2 не находит в этих сохранённых HTML структурированный Agent payload. Это не доказывает, что живой запрос экспортёра сломан: сохранённая страница после загрузки браузером — не обязательно тот же ответ сервера, который экспортёр получает при запросе с активной сессией.

Самой последней версии скрипта в `chat-archive` нет — там сейчас только `Desktop.rar`; в `all-my-chats/main` скрипта тоже нет, а PR с v2.2 закрыт без слияния. Поэтому **именно вашу последнюю правку я подтвердить не могу**. Для полной проверки пришлите текущий `.user.js` и JSON/TXT, полученные экспортёром для одной из этих Agent-сессий — тогда их можно будет сравнить с исходной страницей.

Файлы в текущей ветке я не менял. Отдельно: `chat-archive` публичный, а в сохранённых страницах видны адрес аккаунта и непрозрачные строки, похожие на токен/сессионные данные. Я не цитирую их и не проверял, действительны ли они; если архив не должен быть публичным, стоит проверить его содержимое и при необходимости отозвать активные сессии.

- All 280 `web_search` descriptions are absent; six results beyond the first eight are also omitted.

The test files were enough; **no extra prep is needed**. The distinction is that the **JSON export captured the tool data**, while the **TXT formatter drops much of it**.

For the three manual copies:
- **Page 2** (`Можешь посмотреть…`) has five `fetch_page` results in its JSON export, but I found none of those response bodies in the manual copy—not even sampled excerpts. The copy may contain the assistant’s summary, not the pages it read.
- **Pages 1 and 3** don’t contain `fetch_page`, `read_file`, or `web_search` results, so they don’t back up those outputs.

Across the 17-session test batch, the JSON contains the `fetch_page`, `read_file`, and `web_search` data that the TXT omits. That makes the omissions **not a problem if you keep the JSON**. They do matter if you want the TXT or manual copies to be a self-contained archive: pages can change or disappear, and local files may no longer be available. Search snippets are less critical than the fetched-page and read-file contents, but they’re still useful for checking what informed a response.

So my verdict: **v2.2 is working well for capturing these sessions in JSON, but its TXT output is not lossless.** Keep the JSON as the archive of record; if you want complete standalone TXT too, the formatter needs changes and another test run. Separately, this ZIP has 17 sessions; if that was meant to be your full history rather than a test selection, it’s only a subset.
any possible improvement?

Yes. **The main improvement is in TXT formatting, not Agent Mode parsing**: the JSON exports are capturing the tool data, but the TXT formatter drops much of it.

I’d prioritize:

1. **Include tool response bodies** for `fetch_page` and `read_file`.
2. **Keep every `web_search` result**, including descriptions/snippets—not just the first eight titles and URLs.
3. **Show truncation explicitly** in TXT when Arena marks a Bash output as truncated.
4. **Add a batch manifest** with selected/exported/failed counts, so it’s clear whether a 17-chat ZIP is an intentional sample or a partial history export.
5. Optionally, **archive attachment files themselves** or warn that exported URLs may expire.

I’d leave v2.2 unchanged as your baseline and make these changes in a separate **v2.3** file, then rerun the same test ZIPs. Want me to implement that?

gh pr edit 1 --title "Add Arena exporter v2.2 baseline and v2.3 improvements" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- Keep v2.2 unchanged as the baseline and add a separate v2.3 userscript.
- v2.3 TXT now preserves Agent tool inputs and outputs, including full `fetch_page`/`read_file` bodies, every `web_search` result and description, and explicit notices when upstream truncation flags are present.
- Selected-history exports (including a one-chat selection) are ZIPs containing `manifest.json` with selected/success/failed counts and per-item results. If every chat fails, a manifest-only ZIP is still produced.
- Attachment binaries are not downloaded. JSON/TXT exports and the manifest warn that attachment links may expire or require an active Arena session.
- Keep “Select agent” as an optional convenience filter for quickly selecting Agent Mode chats; it is not required for export correctness.

## Validation
- `node --check` passes for v2.3.
- Replayed the formatter against the 17 Agent JSON records in the existing sample ZIPs: verified 100 `fetch_page` bodies, 17 `read_file` bodies, all 280 web-search results, and 14 stdout-truncation notices.
- Tested nested tool payloads, generic upstream truncation flags, and batch manifests for mixed success/failure, a single selected chat, and all-failed batches.
- Confirmed the v2.2 file remains unchanged.

## Test boundary
The sample ZIPs predate v2.3; their JSON payloads were used to test the new formatter offline. A fresh browser export with v2.3 is still needed for a live end-to-end UI/ZIP check.
EOF
)"

Готово: добавил отдельный userscript v2.3, **v2.2 оставил без изменений**.

- TXT теперь сохраняет полные тела `fetch_page` и `read_file`, все результаты `web_search` с описаниями и остальные поля ввода/вывода инструментов. Маркеры upstream truncation явно отмечаются.
- ZIP для выбранных чатов содержит `manifest.json` со счётчиками выбранных, успешных и неуспешных экспортов. Даже при выборе одного чата создаётся ZIP; если все экспорты не удались, ZIP содержит только манифест.
- В TXT, JSON и манифесте есть предупреждение: файлы вложений не скачиваются, а ссылки на них могут истечь или требовать активной сессии Arena. Это выбранное поведение v2.3.
- Кнопку **Select agent** оставил: для корректного экспорта она не нужна, но позволяет быстро выбрать только чаты Agent Mode.

Проверил форматтер на 17 Agent JSON-записях из существующих ZIP-образцов: подтвердились 100 тел `fetch_page`, 17 тел `read_file`, все 280 результатов поиска и 14 маркеров усечения stdout. Также прошли проверки манифеста для смешанных результатов, одного выбранного чата и полного сбоя. `node --check` проходит.

import zipfile,json,re,collections,os
from pathlib import Path
root=Path('check this out/export attempt')
jsonzip=next(root.glob('*json*.zip'))
txtzip=next(root.glob('*txt*.zip'))

def read_zip(zpath):
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zpath) as z:
        return {Path(n).name: z.read(n) for n in z.namelist() if not n.endswith('/')}

jfiles=read_zip(jsonzip); tfiles=read_zip(txtzip)
print(f'JSON ZIP entries: {len(jfiles)}; TXT ZIP entries: {len(tfiles)}; JSON manifest: {"manifest.json" in jfiles}; TXT manifest: {"manifest.json" in tfiles}')
json_by_id={}
json_stats=collections.Counter(); tool_types=collections.Counter()
for name,data in jfiles.items():
    if not name.lower().endswith('.json'): continue
    try: wrapper=json.loads(data)
    except Exception: json_stats['invalid_json']+=1; continue
    json_stats['json_files']+=1
    rec=wrapper.get('agent') or wrapper.get('evaluation') or {}
    rid=str(rec.get('id') or '')
    if rid: json_by_id[rid]=rec
    json_stats['record_type_'+str(wrapper.get('recordType','unknown'))]+=1
    messages=rec.get('messages') or []
    json_stats['messages']+=len(messages)
    for m in messages:
      for p in m.get('parts') or []:
        typ=str(p.get('type') or 'unknown'); tool_types[typ]+=1
        if typ.startswith('tool-') or typ=='dynamic-tool': json_stats['tool_parts']+=1
        if typ=='tool-fetch_page' and isinstance((p.get('output') or {}).get('content'),str) and (p['output']['content']): json_stats['fetch_page_bodies']+=1
        if typ=='tool-read_file' and isinstance((p.get('output') or {}).get('content'),str) and (p['output']['content']): json_stats['read_file_bodies']+=1
        if typ=='tool-web_search' and isinstance((p.get('output') or {}).get('results'),list):
          json_stats['web_search_calls']+=1; json_stats['web_search_result_items']+=len(p['output']['results'])
          json_stats['web_search_descriptions']+=sum(1 for r in p['output']['results'] if isinstance(r,dict) and isinstance(r.get('description'),str) and r['description'])
        out=p.get('output') or {}
        if isinstance(out,dict):
          json_stats['stdout_trunc_flags']+=int(out.get('stdout_truncated') is True)
          json_stats['stderr_trunc_flags']+=int(out.get('stderr_truncated') is True)

matched=0; no_match=0; txt_stats=collections.Counter(); missing_fetch=missing_read=missing_web_desc=0; missing_stdout=0; trunc_marked=0
for name,data in tfiles.items():
    if not name.lower().endswith('.txt'): continue
    text=data.decode('utf-8-sig','replace')
    txt_stats['txt_files']+=1
    id_match=re.search(r'/agent/([0-9a-f-]{36})',text,re.I)
    if not id_match:
      no_match+=1; continue
    rid=id_match.group(1); rec=json_by_id.get(rid)
    if not rec: no_match+=1; continue
    matched+=1
    txt_stats['matched_txt_files']+=1
    expected_msgs=len(rec.get('messages') or [])
    m=re.search(r'^Messages\s*:\s*(\d+)\s*$',text,re.M)
    if m and int(m.group(1))==expected_msgs: txt_stats['message_counts_match']+=1
    for message in rec.get('messages') or []:
      for p in message.get('parts') or []:
        typ=str(p.get('type') or '')
        out=p.get('output') or {}
        if typ=='tool-fetch_page' and isinstance(out,dict) and isinstance(out.get('content'),str) and out['content']:
          if out['content'] in text: txt_stats['fetch_bodies_present']+=1
          else: missing_fetch+=1
        if typ=='tool-read_file' and isinstance(out,dict) and isinstance(out.get('content'),str) and out['content']:
          if out['content'] in text: txt_stats['read_file_bodies_present']+=1
          else: missing_read+=1
        if typ=='tool-web_search' and isinstance(out,dict) and isinstance(out.get('results'),list):
          for r in out['results']:
            if isinstance(r,dict) and r.get('description'):
              if r['description'] in text: txt_stats['web_search_descriptions_present']+=1
              else: missing_web_desc+=1
        if typ=='tool-bash' and isinstance(out,dict):
          if out.get('stdout_truncated') is True and 'stdout was truncated before export' in text: trunc_marked+=1
          if isinstance(out.get('stdout'),str) and out['stdout'] and out['stdout'] in text: txt_stats['bash_stdout_present']+=1
    if 'attachment links may expire' in text.lower() or 'links may expire' in text.lower() or 'ссылк' in text.lower(): txt_stats['attachment_warning_present']+=1

print('JSON payload summary:',json.dumps(dict(json_stats),sort_keys=True))
print('Tool part types:',json.dumps(dict(tool_types),sort_keys=True))
print('TXT comparison:',json.dumps({**dict(txt_stats),'matched_agent_id_txt_files':matched,'unmatched_txt_files':no_match,'fetch_bodies_missing':missing_fetch,'read_file_bodies_missing':missing_read,'web_search_descriptions_missing':missing_web_desc,'stdout_truncation_notices_found_for_flags':trunc_marked},sort_keys=True))

gh api repos/UselessMoron123/chat-archive/pulls/1 -X PATCH -f body="$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- Keep v2.2 unchanged as the baseline; add the refined v2.3.1 exporter.
- Remove the Agent-only selection button and Chinese localization (English-only UI).
- TXT preserves recorded Agent tool inputs/outputs and marks partial `fetch_page` chunks, limited `read_file` excerpts, tool errors, upstream truncation, and metadata-only image reads. Message timestamps are included when present.
- Selected-history ZIPs include `manifest.json` with selected/success/failed counts and item lists. ZIPs use DEFLATE level 6. Attachment binaries are not downloaded; exports warn that links may expire.
- Tool results are archived as recorded; missing chunks, file ranges, or image bytes are not re-fetched.

## Audit of the newly uploaded v2.3.1 ZIPs
- Both manifests report 17 selected, 17 successful, 0 failed. The JSON and TXT archives each contain the same 16 Agent records plus one regular chat; all 17 IDs and message counts match (125 messages total).
- All JSON records are valid. TXT includes all 100 recorded `fetch_page` bodies, all 21 non-empty `read_file` bodies, all 280 search results, and all 15 stdout-truncation notices.
- All expected completeness notices are present: 63 `fetch_page` responses with `hasMore`, 20 limited `read_file` excerpts, one image read with metadata but no bytes, and two tool-call errors. There are also 10 attachment references without binary data; attachment warnings are included.
- The uploaded ZIPs are actually DEFLATE-compressed: JSON is 1.54 MB (5.94 MB uncompressed) and TXT is 1.49 MB (5.30 MB uncompressed), about 74% and 72% smaller respectively.

## Validation
- `node --check` passes.
- Checked the real v2.3.1 ZIP contents against their manifests and cross-matched every JSON/TXT record, ID, and message count.
- Verified the actual TXT contains the complete serialized search-result arrays plus the fetched/read content and all partial/error markers.
- The v2.2 baseline remains unchanged.
EOF
)"

Confirmed—the new ZIPs were generated by **v2.3.1**, and the actual exports check out.

- Both manifests report **17 selected, 17 successful, 0 failed**. Each ZIP has 17 chat files plus `manifest.json`; all JSON records are valid, and all 17 JSON/TXT pairs match by chat ID and message count (**125 messages total**).
- TXT preserves all **100** recorded `fetch_page` bodies, **21** non-empty `read_file` bodies, all **280** web-search results, and all **15** stdout-truncation notices.
- The new notices are present too: **63** partial `fetch_page` responses, **20** `read_file` excerpts, one image read with metadata but no bytes, and two tool-call errors. These are limitations or errors in the recorded tool results—not failed chat exports.
- The ZIPs use DEFLATE compression: JSON is **1.54 MB** from **5.94 MB** uncompressed; TXT is **1.49 MB** from **5.30 MB**. The attachment warning is included.

**Conclusion:** no missing chat records or JSON/TXT mismatches found. What isn’t present is source data the tools didn’t return—remaining page chunks, unrequested file lines, image bytes, and attachment binaries. The current notices make those limits visible rather than implying they were recovered. I updated PR #1 with this audit.
